featured_reviews.name: Loyson Louis
featured_reviews.review_text:
Baba Falooda – Sitladevi Mandir Metro (Personal Review)
Rating: 2.5–3/5
What I liked:
Rich and generous faloodas loaded with rose syrup, sabja seeds, ice cream, kulfi pieces, and other toppings.
Fresh juices are decent.
The staff appear to make a sincere effort to maintain cleanliness despite being a roadside outlet.
Convenient if you're in the area and craving something cold and sweet.
What I didn't like:
No seating at all; everything is standing-room only.
Being a roadside stall, the entire preparation and serving area is exposed to traffic, dust, and pedestrians.
Presentation is basic—ingredients are packed into the glass without much finesse, and you practically have to "excavate" your falooda with a plastic spoon.
Prices are on the higher side (around ₹100+ per serving).
The constant presence of beggars approaching customers while they're eating can make the experience uncomfortable, especially when dining with a group.
Better alternatives nearby:
Badshah – Better ambience, seating, air-conditioned comfort, and a more enjoyable overall experience for falooda and cold beverages.
Gupta Kulfi Centre – Located opposite Baba Falooda, with air-conditioning and a more comfortable environment, even though space is limited.
Verdict: If you're thirsty and happen to be passing by, Baba Falooda can satisfy a craving for a rich, heavily loaded falooda. However, if comfort, ambience, presentation, and a relaxed experience matter to you, I'd personally choose Badshah ( Crawford market ) or the nearby Gupta Kulfi Centre instead.
"Good in an emergency, but not a destination I'd specifically visit for a falooda."

featured_reviews.name: Alfie Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text: Tried the falooda based on the reviews, it was tasty, full of ice-cream blocks, generous milky syrup, priced well, it seems it gets very crowded in the evening, but when I saw the way ice-cream blocks were cut without any gloves and on cardboard covers, lacked basic hygiene, it was closed to the shewarna grill, not sure if meat and ice cream are stored in the same freezer, but that's what you get in Mumbai street food, full of flavours but be missing hygiene

featured_reviews.name: PD
featured_reviews.review_text:
I will let you in on a secret, whenever your partner is angry with you, take home a bowl of the rich goodness...the kulfi Rabdi bowl.... guarantee heart melting stuff ...can get you out of any kind of trouble
Baba Falooda’s special Malai Kulfi with Rabdi is pure indulgence. The kulfi is dense, creamy, and perfectly set — rich without being overly sweet — and the rabdi layered on top is thick, luscious, and full of that slow-cooked, caramelized milk flavor that feels nostalgic and comforting.
Every spoonful tastes premium and freshly prepared. The portion size is generous, the quality is consistent, and the balance of sweetness is just right. Whether you’re celebrating, apologizing, or simply craving something decadent, this bowl delivers every single time.
If you love traditional Indian desserts done right, Baba Falooda’s Malai Kulfi Rabdi is a must-try. Absolute heart-melting goodness.

featured_reviews.name: The Beekeeper
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Irani Chai in Mahim scores high on location and accessibility. It’s conveniently situated with easy access from Mahim railway station, and the connecting road makes local transport readily available—definitely a plus for first-time visitors or those exploring the area.

As a visitor, I was keen to try this place given its popularity and the buzz around its Irani-style offerings. The preparation style is indeed quite unique and different from what we usually get in the Delhi NCR region, which adds to the curiosity and appeal. However, when it comes to taste, nothing really stood out as mind-blowing.

The place is famous for its concept and the uniqueness of dishes on offer, but the flavours and aroma didn’t quite live up to the hype. I tried a fairly wide spread—Bun Maska, Mutton Keema, Irani Deluxe Chicken Cheese Burger, Veg Cheese Burger, and Paneer Bhurji. Among all of these, the Chicken Cheese Burger was the most flavourful and enjoyable. The rest of the dishes, unfortunately, felt quite average.

One thing to note is that all dishes—whether gravy-based or dry—are served with pav (if needed). You won’t find rotis or parathas here, which aligns with the Irani café concept.

Overall, Cafe Irani Chai is worth a one-time visit if you’re keen on trying something that’s quite famous and culturally distinct. But from a taste perspective, it didn’t leave a lasting impression and isn’t something i would consider a go-to place.

featured_reviews.name: Hrishikesh Chinchalikar
featured_reviews.review_text:
🌴 A Heartwarming Goan Experience at a Portuguese Restaurant 🌴

Dining at this Goan Portuguese restaurant was truly a delightful experience. From the first bite to the last note of live music, everything felt authentic, soulful, and unforgettable.

The food was absolutely amazing—rich in flavor, perfectly balanced, and deeply rooted in Goan tradition. Every dish reflected care, passion, and mastery of recipes passed down through generations.

⭐ Special Dishes We Tried:

Coconut Cashew Bhaji – A standout vegetarian dish, creamy, mildly spiced, and incredibly comforting. The coconut and cashew combination was simply delicious.

Surmai Fish Kalvam – A must-try for fish lovers. Fresh surmai cooked in a flavorful Goan-style curry that was bold, aromatic, and unforgettable.

Live Music by Uncle – The soulful live music added magic to the evening, creating a warm and joyful Goan vibe that elevated the entire dining experience.

What truly made this place special was the personal touch. The owner personally visited every table, warmly sharing the inspiring journey of how the restaurant began. He spoke about his wife’s culinary journey and her exceptional talent as a cook—the heart behind the delicious recipes served here. Listening to their story made the food taste even better, knowing it comes from passion, dedication, and love.

The restaurant has grown into multiple branches, including international locations, and it’s easy to see why. This place is not just about food—it’s about culture, stories, and genuine hospitality.

✨ Highly recommended for anyone who loves authentic Goan cuisine, soulful music, and heartfelt hospitality. A place you’ll want to visit again and again.

featured_reviews.name: Leena Surve
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goa Portuguese is a must stop in my every visit to Mumbai (from USA). This place has such a fun vibe with awesome food. There Goan and malvani dishes remind me of my mom’s home cooking.   We always start with Bombay duck fry and shrimp koliwada. Then the order including tisarya sukhe, chicken xacuti, pomfret / surmai dishes, amboli, vade continues so much that we get warned by the waiter ‘jara jast hoil ho’ (might be little to much). But we love their food so much that the warning, even though correct, gets ignored.
Even after visiting so many times, we have managed to touch very less amounts of dishes offered. Must increase our visits.
This time was lucky to meet with Dr. Suhas Awchat (co-founder). A warm personality and all the praise for master chef, Mrs. Deepa Awchat (he openly gave the credit of starting and owning the restaurant completely  to her, indicating that after army, she is his boss 😀).
Awesome food, fun atmosphere, good - helpful staff. Definitely a must visit place.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Jaffer Bhai! Delhi Darbar offers a mixed experience, but the food is definitely the star of the show. We tried the Raan and Butter Chicken, and they were super yummy! The dishes are bursting with flavor and truly live up to the Delhi Darbar name. Each bite is a delightful exploration of spices and textures, leaving you craving more.

However, the dining experience is somewhat marred by other factors. Parking is a significant hurdle. Finding a spot can be incredibly challenging, adding unnecessary stress to your visit. Be prepared to spend some time circling the block or consider alternative transportation.

The service, unfortunately, doesn't quite match the quality of the food. While the staff is polite, their energy and enthusiasm seem to be lacking. A more attentive and vibrant service would greatly enhance the overall atmosphere.

In conclusion, Jaffer Bhai! Delhi Darbar is a place where the food shines, especially the Raan and Butter Chicken. However, the overall experience is somewhat diminished by parking difficulties and less-than-stellar service. If you're willing to overlook these drawbacks for the sake of the delicious food, it's worth a visit.

Hotel Saibini Gomantak is a true gem for anyone who loves authentic, flavorful food. The highlight of the menu is undoubtedly their thalis, each one packed with rich malvani taste and generous portions.

The Chicken Thali stands out with its perfectly spiced gravy, tender pieces of chicken, and a balanced combination of sides that make every bite satisfying. The Mutton Thali is equally impressive—slow-cooked mutton that is juicy, aromatic, and full of depth, making it a must-try for meat lovers. If you enjoy seafood, the Prawns Thali is exceptional, featuring fresh prawns cooked to perfection in a delicious, coastal-style curry that brings out traditional flavors beautifully.

The overall experience is enhanced by the homely touch in the cooking, quick service, and consistent quality. Hotel Saibini Gomantak is definitely a go-to place if you’re craving hearty, delicious thalis that truly capture the essence of local konkan cuisine.
